stem: Release engineers sign in to a development account through a federated role. For deployments they need short-lived access to a separate production account, and no identities may be created for them in production. Which TWO steps are required? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: In development, edit the trust policy of the engineers' role to name the production deployment role as a trusted entity
In production, create a deployment role whose trust policy names the development account as a trusted principal
Set up VPC peering between the two accounts so that the release engineers can reach production resources
In development, allow the engineers' role to call sts:AssumeRole on the production deployment role's ARN
Add the development account's release role to an IAM group in the production account

rationale: Cross-account role access needs both sides: a role in the destination account whose trust policy names the originating account, and an identity-based policy in the originating account that allows sts:AssumeRole on that role's ARN. AssumeRole then returns temporary credentials. A trust policy belongs on the role being assumed, in production, not on the role doing the assuming in development; every role already has exactly one trust policy, and editing the one on the development-side role does not grant it permission to call sts:AssumeRole on the production role, and production would still lack a role that trusts the development account. VPC peering connects networks; it does not grant any IAM permissions. IAM groups contain only IAM users of the same account, so a role from another account cannot be added.
